name: Heart Transplant (cardiac transplant, heart replacement)

category.name: Heart
category.part: AME Physical Examination Information and Disposition Tables

what_to_bring: Submit the following for FAA review: The most recent detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with their cardiologist or cardiac surgeon which verifies the transplant has been performed.
A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating cardiologist or transplant surgeon no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam.
It must specifically include:
Any evidence of rejection and complete documentation of all rejection history, whether treated or not;
A complete history regarding any infectious process;
A complete history regarding any malignancy; and
Comment on the donor heart status, including any evidence of allograft vasculopathy or any disease state.
Labs performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam:
Hemoglobin A1C and
Lipid profile to include total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides.
Hospital records to include:
Operative report;
Discharge summary from the physician (NOT the discharge instructions/paperwork given to the patient when leaving the hospital);
Admission (history & physical);
Pathology report (if performed); and
DO NOT submit miscellaneous hospital records such as flowsheets, nursing notes, physician orders, and medication administration records.
Coronary Angiogram [cardiac cath] performed no more than 12 months before the AME exam:
Must submit both of the report(s); and
Actual imaging on CD in DICOM format.
24-hour cardiac monitor performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam:
Stress Echo . Graded Exercise Stress ECHO (with electrical tracings) no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam in accordance with the enclosed specification sheet.
Any other testing already completed or deemed necessary by the treating physician (e.g., myocardial biopsy)

rows.label: B
rows.evaluation_data: There is NO mandatory recovery period per Public Law 114-190 May 2017, but should be released by the treating physician. After the treating cardiologist and/or transplant surgeon has determined that the condition is stable, obtain the following evaluation(s) and submit them to the FAA for review: - 1. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating cardiologist or transplant surgeon no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam. It should include a summary of the history of the condition or diagnosis; current medications, dosages, and side effects (if any); clinical exam findings; results of any testing performed; diagnosis; assessment and plan (prognosis); and follow-up. - 2. It must specifically include: - A statement regarding functional capacity, modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, and prognosis for incapacitation; - Any evidence of rejection and complete documentation of all rejection history, whether treated or not; - A complete history regarding any infectious process; - A complete history regarding any malignancy; and - Comment on the donor heart status, including any evidence of allograft vasculopathy or any disease state. - 3. Labs performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam: - Hemoglobin A1C and - Lipid profile to include total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides. - 4. Hospital records to include: - Operative report; - Discharge summary from the physician (NOT the discharge instructions/paperwork given to the patient when leaving the hospital); - Admission (history & physical); - Pathology report (if performed); and - DO NOT submit miscellaneous hospital records such as flowsheets, nursing notes, physician orders, and medication administration records. - 5. Coronary Angiogram [cardiac cath] performed no more than 12 months before the AME exam: - Must submit both of the report(s); and - Actual imaging on CD in DICOM format. - 6. 24-hour cardiac monitor performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam: ≥ 24-hour cardiac monitor (such as a Holter, Zio Patch, etc.). It should include atrial and ventricular ectopic counts; hourly tabular data to include the longest pause duration and counts of all pauses 2.5 seconds or greater; heart rate (max, min, and average); other histograms and frequency graphs; and the percentage of atrial fibrillation/flutter. - 7. Stress Echo. Graded Exercise Stress ECHO (with electrical tracings) no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam in accordance with the enclosed specification sheet. - 8. Any other testing already completed or deemed necessary by the treating physician (e.g., myocardial biopsy)
rows.evaluation_data_html:
There is NO mandatory recovery period per Public Law 114-190 May 2017, but should be released by the treating physician.

After the treating cardiologist and/or transplant surgeon has determined that the condition is stable, obtain the following evaluation(s) and submit them to the FAA for review:

  • 1. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating cardiologist or transplant surgeon no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam.

It should include a summary of the history of the condition or diagnosis; current medications, dosages, and side effects (if any); clinical exam findings; results of any testing performed; diagnosis; assessment and plan (prognosis); and follow-up.

  • 2. It must specifically include:

    • A statement regarding functional capacity, modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, and prognosis for incapacitation;
    • Any evidence of rejection and complete documentation of all rejection history, whether treated or not;
    • A complete history regarding any infectious process;
    • A complete history regarding any malignancy; and
    • Comment on the donor heart status, including any evidence of allograft vasculopathy or any disease state.
  • 3. Labs performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam:
  • Hemoglobin A1C and
  • Lipid profile to include total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides.
  • 4. Hospital records to include:
  • Operative report;
  • Discharge summary from the physician (NOT the discharge instructions/paperwork given to the patient when leaving the hospital);
  • Admission (history & physical);
  • Pathology report (if performed); and
  • DO NOT submit miscellaneous hospital records such as flowsheets, nursing notes, physician orders, and medication administration records.
  • 5. Coronary Angiogram [cardiac cath] performed no more than 12 months before the AME exam:
  • Must submit both of the report(s); and
  • Actual imaging on CD in DICOM format.
  • 6. 24-hour cardiac monitor performed no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam:

≥ 24-hour cardiac monitor (such as a Holter, Zio Patch, etc.). It should include atrial and ventricular ectopic counts; hourly tabular data to include the longest pause duration and counts of all pauses 2.5 seconds or greater; heart rate (max, min, and average); other histograms and frequency graphs; and the percentage of atrial fibrillation/flutter.

  • 7. Stress Echo. Graded Exercise Stress ECHO (with electrical tracings) no more than 90 days prior to the AME exam in accordance with the enclosed specification sheet.
  • 8. Any other testing already completed or deemed necessary by the treating physician (e.g., myocardial biopsy)
